Investment announcements, asset transfers and construction spending can describe different stages or overlapping money. This research adds six named IMFA and NALCO project/phase records so shared company and place names cannot collapse them into one project or inflate an investment total.

- IMFA: distinguish the completed KNR2 purchase, its unimplemented fifth furnace and separate KNR1 construction. Retain ₹707.27 crore reported payment, ₹610 crore base consideration and ₹25.03 crore assumed working capital as overlapping scopes with an unresolved payment bridge.

Odisha’s mining story needs to distinguish mineral income from budgets, funded assets from working services, and research facilities from commercial production. This research connects audited public receipts and DMF cases with mine rights, environmental monitoring, safety and mineral innovation.

- **Public money and services:** the completed RES-053 desk deliverable contains six annual audited receipt observations, six sampled district fund tables and 23 dated project/programme cases. Allocations, expenditure, completion and observed function remain separate. Government responses, uncovered villages and unresolved financial differences are retained; there is no combined loss total.
- **Rights, environment and safety:** RES-054 covers the Niyamgiri court and village-decision evidence, Kodingamali rehabilitation reporting, the Bharatpur 2019 accident and Baphlimali monitoring. Proposed diversion is not actual clearing; planted areas do not establish survival or ecological recovery. Company claims, audit findings and parliamentary reports retain their attribution. Pollution units, monitoring denominators, raw annexures and later legal or corrective-action status remain explicit gaps, with retry dates.
- **History and mineral research:** RES-055 adds one canonical RRL/IMMT account, four primary sources and nine historical/project-stage records. Battery and fly-ash processes retain bench-scale descriptions and institution-reported readiness levels. July 2025 inaugurations, a foundation stone and an upcoming platinum-group pilot are recorded separately. A named researcher’s professional Odisha connection does not imply birthplace, regional identity or sole invention. Talcher’s Census chronology and Rourkela’s existing chain now add seventeen typed historical events from four new sources and one reused mine report. Lease dates, production starts, furnace firing, dedication and capacity-phase completion remain distinct. The 1961 Census vintage and 1966 publication date are separate. Two scientist profiles now credit Mamata Mohapatra and M.G. Sujana. A selected English review preserves all six coauthors, online and issue dates, and corresponding-author credit. Danida documentation separates the named researcher, grant PI, institutions and grant period from the fellowship visit. Three new publisher/funder sources and one reused institutional profile support this checkpoint. An original journal abstract now credits the Sujana–Anand ferric-hydroxide study. A May 2026 PIB report describes a tour of four named pilot facilities, adding later evidence without proving commercial production or precise equivalence with earlier project names. RES-055’s bounded synthesis is complete. Worker-settlement histories, full methods, patents, project-specific trial reports and measured operating outcomes remain dated follow-ups.

The existing rare-earth journey and science/mining pages are connected rather than duplicated. Source and destination KB inventories are reconciled separately; frozen evidence and unrelated work are preserved. Repeated institutional accounts are not independent corroboration. Failed fetches and conflicting source fields remain visible.
